_comment: Our own ingredient → USDA mapping. A SUPERSET, not an amendment.
usda.db is reference data. It is gitignored, rebuilt by
`bun scripts/build-usda-db.ts`, and never edited: amending it in place would
be destroyed on the next rebuild, and would quietly detach the nutrition
figures from the published USDA release they claim to come from. The whole
value of USDA is that it is citable, and an edited copy is not.
So our knowledge lives here instead, in version control, where each decision
carries a reason and shows up in a diff. Same principle as curated.json
against sources.db: the decision file is tracked, the derived database is
disposable.
Resolution order, first hit wins:
1. an exact `match` in this file
2. a `pattern` in this file (substring, checked longest-first)
3. the full-text search heuristics in to-grams.ts
Fields:
fdcId   — the USDA record to use. Look it up in the admin's USDA foods tab.
A NEGATIVE id names an entry in not-in-usda.json: a food or form USDA lacks.
note    — why this mapping, especially when the obvious match was wrong.
reject  — true to say 'this is not a food' (e.g. 'to taste'), so the
heuristics are not given a chance to invent something.

butter.note: Marry me chicken, 2026-10-24: Butter, salted (SR Legacy, tbsp 14.2 g). '2 tbsp butter' reached it, but '25g (0.9 oz) butter', which needs no portion, reached Foundation's 'Butter, stick, salted', so one food sat on two records (G16).

ground beef.note: Beef, ground, 80% lean / 20% fat, raw. The default for meatloaf; heuristics reached corned beef.

milk.note: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat. Heuristics reached 'Crackers, milk' and 'Milk dessert, frozen'.

egg.note: Egg, whole, raw, fresh. Chosen over the Foundation record because it publishes every size: small 38 g, medium 44, large 50, extra large 56, jumbo 63.

eggs.note: Egg, whole, raw, fresh. Chosen over the Foundation record because it publishes every size: small 38 g, medium 44, large 50, extra large 56, jumbo 63.

large eggs.note: Egg, whole, raw, fresh. Chosen over the Foundation record because it publishes every size: small 38 g, medium 44, large 50, extra large 56, jumbo 63.

garlic.note: Garlic, raw. 'garlic cloves' matched 'Spices, cloves, ground' — the unit word is also a food.

ketchup.note: Catsup. USDA files the cup portion under the older spelling; the 'Ketchup' records carry none.

onion.note: Onions, raw. Carries whole-onion portions: medium 110 g, large 150 g.

yellow onion.note: See onion; 'Onions, yellow, sauteed' is the only yellow record and it is cooked.

celery.note: Celery, raw. Stalk portions: small 17 g, medium 40, large 64.

water.note: Water, bottled, generic. Needed for dough hydration; 'Water, as needed' is still refused via the 'as needed' reject phrase.

all-purpose flour.note: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, bleached.

yeast.note: Leavening agents, yeast, baker's, active dry. Bare 'yeast' otherwise reaches 'Yeast extract spread'.

tomato.note: Tomatoes, crushed, canned — what a pizza-sauce row means by 'tomato' at 28 oz.

red pepper.note: Spices, pepper, red or cayenne — flakes, in a pizza sauce; not a bell pepper.

oil.note: Oil, olive, salad or cooking. A bare 'oil' in a pizza dough.

soy sauce.note: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu), 5493 mg Na/100 g. Heuristics reached 'Sauce, peanut, made from ... soy sauce' at 1338 — a 4x understatement of the saltiest line in the recipe. 'Reduced-sodium soy sauce' is NOT aliased: heuristics find the right record.

bacon.note: Pork, cured, bacon, unprepared. A recipe's bacon goes in raw; the cooked record reads 3x saltier because the water has left. Heuristics reached 'Bacon, meatless'.

chicken broth.note: Soup, chicken broth, ready-to-serve. Cartons are what most recipes mean by broth AND stock; home-made stock carries under half the sodium, so a recipe that says so reads high. Heuristics reached 'Chicken, canned, no broth'.

beef broth.note: Soup, beef broth or bouillon canned, ready-to-serve. Cartons are what most recipes mean by broth AND stock; home-made stock carries under half the sodium, so a recipe that says so reads high. Heuristics reached 'Soup, stock, beef, home-prepared'.

vegetable broth.note: Soup, vegetable broth, ready to serve. The generic record; heuristics reached the SWANSON branded one.

sugar.note: Garlic noodles, 2026-09-30: Sugars, granulated, which publishes tsp and cup. With a household measure, heuristics reached 'Sugars, brown' because it publishes a tbsp portion and granulated does not.

white sugar.note: See sugar. Heuristics reached the survey record 'Sugar, white, granulated or lump', whose portions did not convert a teaspoon.

carrot.note: Carrots, raw (SR, nine portions). Foundation's tie-break picked 'Carrots, baby, raw' for a plain carrot (G15, Zaragoza picadillo).

baby carrot.note: Carrots, baby, raw. Keeps baby carrots off the plain 'carrot' pattern above.

yukon gold.note: Potatoes, gold, without skin, raw. 'yukon' is not in the index, so the fallback searched 'potatoes' alone and found red (G15).

castelvetrano.note: Olives, pickled, canned or bottled, green. Castelvetrano is a green olive; the fallback reached a pimiento-stuffed Manzanilla (G15).

ancho chile.note: Peppers, ancho, dried. USDA files chiles under 'Peppers'; the fallback reached 'Chiles rellenos' (G25). Not bare 'ancho': that is inside 'anchovy'.

guajillo.note: STAND-IN: USDA has no guajillo. Peppers, hot chile, sun-dried is the nearest dried red chile (G25).

canela.note: Spices, cinnamon, ground. Canela is Ceylon cinnamon; USDA does not separate it from cassia (G26).

mexican oregano.note: STAND-IN: Spices, oregano, dried. Mexican oregano is Lippia graveolens, a different plant USDA does not list (G26).

ground meat.note: 'Ground meat, such as beef, pork, veal…': raw ground beef, the usual choice. Heuristics reached the survey food 'Meat, ground, NFS', which is cooked and salted (382 mg sodium per 100 g against 66).

bread crumb.note: Bread, crumbs, dry, grated, plain. Covers breadcrumb, bread crumbs, Italian bread crumbs.

kosher salt.note: Salt, table. Kosher differs by crystal size, not composition.

black pepper.note: Spices, pepper, black. Heuristics reached 'Peppers, bell, red, raw'.

olive oil.note: Oil, olive, salad or cooking. Covers extra virgin.

grated parmesan.note: Cheese, parmesan, grated — the record with a cup portion (100 g). Heuristics reached 'parmesan, hard', which has none, so a cup of cheese weighed nothing.

parmesan.note: Garlic noodles, 2026-09-30: Cheese, parmesan, grated (cup 100 g, tbsp 5 g, oz). Recipes measure parmesan by volume, so they mean grated; heuristics reached 'Cheese, parmesan, hard', which publishes no cup and left the line with no weight.

parmigiano.note: See parmesan. 'Parmigiano Reggiano' found no match at all.

neutral oil.note: Garlic noodles, 2026-09-30: Oil, canola, the named default for a generic 'neutral oil' (G15). Heuristics reached 'Oil, oat' and, with a stated mass, 'Oil, corn'.

fish sauce.note: Garlic noodles, 2026-09-30: Sauce, fish, ready-to-serve. Covers brand-prefixed lines: 'Son Fish Sauce' reached 'Sauce, barbecue'.

red pepper flakes.note: Garlic noodles, 2026-09-30: Spices, pepper, red or cayenne. 'crushed red pepper flakes' reached 'Onions, dehydrated flakes'.

noodle water.note: Garlic noodles, 2026-09-30: Beverages, water, tap, drinking. Reserved cooking water; 'pasta or noodle water' reached 'Water convolvulus, raw', a leafy green. Carries the pot's salt in reality, which no record can know.

spaghetti.note: Garlic noodles, 2026-09-30: Pasta, dry, enriched (cup of spaghetti 91 g, 2 oz 57 g). Recipes weigh spaghetti dry; heuristics reached 'Spaghetti, spinach, dry' and 'Ramen bowl, NFS'. A line naming spaghetti as one alternative of several takes this too (G21).

sun noodle.note: Garlic noodles, 2026-09-30: fresh ramen (Sun Noodle is a brand), counted as dry pasta by dry matter (G22). The line's 'or substitute dried spaghetti' must not make it dry pasta at face mass.

organic sugar.note: See sugar. Chef Tu's 'Organic Sugar [1/2 tsp Monk Fruit Sugar]' reached 'Sugars, brown'.

green onion.note: Garlic noodles, 2026-09-30: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb), raw — the record 'scallion' already reaches. 'green onions' reached 'Onions, young green, tops only', so one food under two names split across two records and never reached consensus (G16).

maggi seasoning.note: Garlic noodles, 2026-09-30: not in the USDA datasets we load; our spec in not-in-usda.json cites the Branded Foods record. Heuristics reached 'Seasoning mix, dry, taco, original' (G23).

fresh egg noodles.note: Garlic noodles, 2026-09-30: counted as dry egg noodles by dry matter (G22); heuristics reached the fried 'Noodles, chinese, chow mein' at 1.6% water.

fresh pre-cooked chow mein.note: Garlic noodles, 2026-09-30: steamed fresh noodles, not the fried canned kind; counted as dry pasta by dry matter (G22), an overstatement for a pre-cooked noodle.

chicken breast.note: Marry me chicken, 2026-10-24: Chicken, broiler or fryers, breast, skinless, boneless, meat only, raw (1 piece = 272 g). 'boneless, skinless chicken breasts' reached 'Pork, fresh, loin, blade (chops), boneless' and '4 chicken breasts' reached 'Chicken breast, roll, oven-roasted', a deli meat. The backbone of the dish converted in none of eight recipes (G29).

heavy cream.note: Marry me chicken, 2026-10-24: Cream, fluid, heavy whipping. Already the heuristic match; pinned so the cream every recipe uses cannot drift to 'light (coffee cream)', which '¾ cup 177 ml heavy cream' reached.

double cream.note: Marry me chicken, 2026-10-24: Cream, fluid, heavy whipping. British double cream is about 48% fat against heavy cream's 36%; USDA has no double cream, and heavy is the nearest. It had reached 'Cream, fluid, light (coffee cream or table cream)', at 20%.

plain flour.note: Marry me chicken, 2026-10-24: = all-purpose flour (Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, bleached). The British and Australian name; heuristics reached 'Snacks, pretzels, hard, plain, made with enriched flour'.

crushed red pepper.note: Marry me chicken, 2026-10-24: Spices, pepper, red or cayenne, as 'red pepper flakes'. 'Simply Organic® Crushed Red Pepper' reached 'Pepper, banana, raw'.

chilli flakes.note: Marry me chicken, 2026-10-24: Spices, pepper, red or cayenne, as 'red pepper flakes'. The British spelling reached 'Onions, dehydrated flakes'.

chili flakes.note: Marry me chicken, 2026-10-24: See chilli flakes; the same miss with one l.

tomatoes in oil.note: Marry me chicken, 2026-10-24: Tomatoes, sun-dried, packed in oil, drained (1 cup = 110 g, twice the dry-packed 54 g). '125g sundried tomatoes in oil, drained' reached 'Oil, corn'.

sundried tomato.note: Marry me chicken, 2026-10-24: Tomatoes, sun-dried. 'sundried' as one word is not the indexed 'sun-dried'. A line that says 'in oil' is caught first by the longer 'tomatoes in oil'.

dried thyme.note: Marry me chicken, 2026-10-24: Spices, thyme, dried. '1/2 teaspoon dried thyme' reached 'Thyme, fresh', 0.4 g where dried is 0.5 g, and split one food across two records.

white wine.note: Marry me chicken (That Dude Can Cook), 2026-10-24: Alcoholic beverage, wine, table, white (fl oz 29 g). '1/2 cup dry white wine' reached 'Wine cooler', with no grams.

dijon.note: Marry me chicken (That Dude Can Cook), 2026-10-24: Mustard, prepared, yellow (tsp 5 g). USDA has no Dijon; prepared yellow mustard is the nearest record and is marked STAND-IN here. '2 tsp Dijon mustard' reached 'Mustard greens, raw', the miss PR #5's note listed for bare mustard.
